excerpt: Learn how our team increased regression test coverage for CMN by 15x and faster defect resolution by leveraging automation.
customer: Children’s Miracle Network Hospitals ® raises funds and awareness for 170 member hospitals that provide 32 million treatments each year to kids across the U.S. and Canada. challenge: The CMN team had a huge concern with the integrity of their data and the validity of business logic within their applications. With over 70 existing web applications and a ratio of about 7.8 projects per employee in the IT department, manual regression tests for all releases were impossible. Additionally, there was also little to no documentation on nearly all of the applications and the team had limited expertise in test automation. The CMN team also conservatively reported that they spend about 30% of their time each day on maintenance related tasks such as redeploying broken builds and stabilizing environments.
approach: Through a series of interviews with the CMN team, our consultants were able to resolve the issues surrounding the lack of documentation by defining project specifications. We were able to seamlessly integrate with the existing teams at CMN which allowed users to perform informal interviews that gave us a better understanding of their entire ecosystem and supplement the lack of documentation.  In order to make the most efficient use of the limited time of the  CMN employees, our consultants examined the existing code base to design our own specifications which were then vetted by the CMN team. Automated Regression Testing With the knowledge gained from the interviews, the QW team created a series of end-to-end testing frameworks using WebdriverIO, TypeScript & MSSQL data integrations along with accompanying reports to give QA and other stakeholders some visibility and confidence for new and existing projects. This resulted in the finding of a large number of bugs before release in the UI and Data layer of their applications. For their database, a ruby-based framework called Slacker was used to manipulate and test aspects of their MSSQL database instance for their Core database. Test automation frameworks were created by our team for their Databases and SSRS reports for their largest production applications. This built confidence in their ability to make changes to their applications without introducing any unwanted functionality. We also enhanced their CI/CD Pipeline to generate reports that would indicate to the team the errors or bugs that may arise with new builds of their existing applications.  These frameworks were handed over to their data team. The team was now able to write, maintain, and execute automation suites and view insightful reports on what was happening which allowed them to fail fast and fix quickly.
outcome: During our engagement, QualityWorks was able fully to automate 13 high-impact applications which were then integrated into their CI/CD pipeline . By moving from no automation to aggressively automating wherever possible, we enabled the team to perform true regression tests which enabled faster and earlier defect identification and resolution. Our solutions resulted in an increase in regression test coverage by 15x. The culture of automation has since been fully embraced by the CMN team in every way, even outside of the engagements that we were originally contracted to perform. They are well equipped to continue the work started by QualityWorks and are significantly more confident with their ability to deliver quality products in a timely manner by leveraging the training, tools, and automated regression testing framework. title: Modernizing Financial Platforms Through Smart Test Automation
excerpt: Discover how QualityWorks helped a leading fintech firm modernize its legacy iPipeline Laser App: cutting regression cycles from 2 weeks to 2 days, achieving 90%+ automation coverage, and reducing QA effort by over 80% across 200–300 client platforms.
customer: QualityWorks partnered with 3CI’s client, a leading financial technology firm, to help overcome a critical modernization challenge. This firm needed to upgrade their legacy Laser App platform that serves 200-300 clients without compromising quality or causing system regressions. Through QualityWorks’ strategic expertise implementation over an 8 month engagement, the firm achieved a remarkable transformation. QualityWorks helped them reduce regression testing cycles from 2 weeks to just 2 days while establishing enterprise-grade QA practices from the ground up, enabling then to modernize their platform with confidence and maintain their high service standards for their extensive client base.
challenge: Before the QualityWorks team began engaging, this fintech faced significant QA-related challenges that threatened the reliability of its core platform. The existing system was built on a legacy tech stack with no prior documentation, test cases, or user stories, making the testing landscape complex and prone to risk. All regression testing was conducted manually, which took up to two weeks per cycle and consumed critical team resources. The lack of automation and structure led to inefficiencies and increased the chance of undetected issues slipping into production. Furthermore, with an impending platform upgrade, stakeholders demanded a high level of confidence in post-deployment stability, but the company lacked the testing infrastructure to provide that assurance.
approach: The QualityWorks team implemented a full QA transformation strategy over an eight-month period by embedding a two-person QA team into their development workflow. The process began with discovery sessions and user flow mapping to create clarity and structure around application behavior. From this foundation, the team developed over 500 detailed test cases and constructed a robust automation framework from scratch. Automation targeted the core functionality of the platform, supporting three key user roles: End-user, Assistant, and Admin. Initially, Playwright was used to build rapid test coverage, but the team later transitioned to Katalon in alignment with client preferences and team familiarity. The automation framework leveraged a modular, data-driven architecture using the Page Object Model to ensure scalability and maintainability. Additional tools such as Azure DevOps and Quality Watcher were integrated for test management and continuous execution, and custom utilities were developed to support dynamic form handling and data-driven reporting dashboards.
outcome: 85% Reduction in Testing Time 90% Automation Coverage 80%+ Work Effort Savings The QA transformation delivered measurable and high-impact results across the board. The regression testing cycle was dramatically reduced from two weeks to just two days, resulting in an 80%+ reduction in manual tester hours and significantly accelerating the release cycle. The automation framework achieved over 90% test coverage, enabling their platform  to execute daily and pull request-based test runs with confidence. Each automated test completed in under a minute, and the full suite of over 500 tests could be executed within two days, a massive improvement from the manual process. Perhaps most notably, their platform experienced a sharp increase in internal stakeholder confidence thanks to the reliability and speed of the new QA pipeline. As one client stakeholder noted, “We were impressed by the team’s adaptability and velocity—50+ automated tests weekly—and their commitment to meeting our standards even while switching tools midstream.” The QA system is now scalable, resilient, and fully aligned with future development and deployment demands. title: Site Reliability Engineering for Major Entertainment Platform
excerpt: Our comprehensive Site Reliability Engineering services ensure your platform maintains exceptional reliability as you scale. From proactive monitoring to automated incident response, we help you build systems that thrive under pressure.
customer: Founded in 2000, Fandango serves approximately 36 million moviegoers each month through their website and mobile app. As the go-to destination for movie tickets, Fandango’s platform must maintain exceptional reliability during high-stakes movie releases where downtime directly impacts revenue and customer experience. The company could see that customer expectations for seamless digital experiences were evolving exponentially. As technology demands increased, Fandango knew it needed to evolve from reactive problem-solving to proactive reliability engineering to secure its position as the industry leader.
challenge: For several consecutive years, peak‑day presales triggered slowdowns and errors that risked revenue and brand reputation. Ahead of Star Wars: The Last Jedi, projections showed traffic could spike to ≈ 85 k concurrent users and 2 million page views per hour. Their ad‑hoc load‑testing tools were expensive to run continuously, observability was limited, and performance issues were often discovered once they had already reached production. Fandango needed an ongoing Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practice capable of predicting capacity needs, surfacing bottlenecks earlier in the pipeline, and embedding reliability into every release.
approach: QualityWorks put in place a comprehensive Site Reliability Engineering program that replaced one‑off performance fixes with a disciplined, end‑to‑end reliability framework. We began with a Reliability Assessment & Monitoring phase, analyzing production traffic and failure patterns to set a clear baseline. From that data we defined service‑level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets for every revenue‑critical user journey, giving product and engineering teams a shared, measurable definition of “good enough.” Next came Proactive Performance Engineering . We stood up a continuous performance‑testing pipeline in Jenkins, AWS, and Ansible that could replay real‑world traffic at scale with a single click. The pipeline quickly exposed—and our team eliminated—six high‑impact bottlenecks across application and database tiers. In parallel, we introduced capacity‑planning playbooks that forecast resource needs ahead of every major film release, turning surprise traffic spikes into predictable events. Finally, we addressed Infrastructure Reliability . We eliminated costly third‑party load‑testing tools and ensured that every code change passes reliability checks in the continuous‑integration pipeline before it reaches production.
outcome: 7x Performance Improvement 80% Faster Response 99.9% Uptime Transformational Reliability Improvements Fandango’s platform can absorb seven times more traffic, effortlessly handling bursts of 85,000+ concurrent users. The new headroom proved itself during the record‑setting Star Wars: The Last Jedi presale which ran without any major hiccups. Subsequent releases have enjoyed the same resilience, sustaining 99.9 percent uptime and removing the revenue risk once tied to blockbuster launch days. Built‑in sustainability keeps those gains growing. Ongoing reliability metrics give leadership clear insight into error‑budget burn‑down and uptime trends, while engineers focus optimization where it delivers the most value. With outages eliminated, Fandango protects every peak‑sales minute, sees customer‑satisfaction scores rise, and benefits from a leaner cloud bill as resources are provisioned precisely to verified demand—reducing operational overhead and freeing teams to ship new features faster. challenge: Founded in 2000, Fandango is one of  America’s largest ticketing companies that sells movie tickets via their website as well as through their mobile app. As the go-to destination for just about 36 million moviegoers each month, Fandango’s web and mobile applications experience significant traffic during major movie releases. For multiple years, during peak sales periods, Fandango’s site has experienced significant performance issues due to the high level of online traffic. In anticipation of Star Wars: The Last Jedi, Fandango needed to be able to scale their platform to manage a potential calculated load of approximately 85,168 concurrent users on mobile and desktop applications. Our team was required to create a full performance test suite to run against all their environments in order to monitor site performance under heavy load and to identify bottlenecks.
approach: Through collaboration with the Fandango team, we were able to assess peak traffic on the production environment and calculate a load of 85,168 concurrent users and an average of 2 Million page views per hour. Using this data, our team was able to: Replicate that same load at a reduced cost based on strategic load tests Prepare proof of concept performance scripts Understand how the system would perform and react under different kinds of pressure Identify six major performance bottlenecks affecting critical applications and database servers. Our team also created an internal performance test environment using Jenkins, AWS & Ansible that significantly reduced the dependency on the more expensive tool, Blazemeter. This solution was not only effective but sustainable as it became a part of their continuous performance testing pipeline, allowing them to easily test the performance of their system before future new movie releases.
outcome: Our performance testing solutions enabled Fandango to optimize their system by a factor of 7x on the basis of performance and scalability. ‘Star Wars: The Last Jedi’ became Fandango’s top advance ticket seller for 2017. title: Speed Meets Purpose: Scaling Volunteer Matching
excerpt: QualityWorks engaged a social enterprise organization staff closely from the early stages of product development to help define the user experience.
customer: Shared Harvest is a purpose-driven social enterprise that bridges the gap between skilled volunteers with student loan debt (Debt freelancers) and mission-based organizations (Changemakers/Harvesters). By facilitating meaningful project-based collaborations, Shared Harvest empowers individuals to reduce student debt through service while supporting causes that matter.
challenge: Shared Harvest Fund set out to build a digital platform that would serve two very distinct user groups — volunteers and nonprofit organizations — each with unique needs and interactions. The organization faced significant technical and operational challenges in creating a solution that could effectively bridge the gap between these diverse stakeholders while maintaining functionality and user satisfaction. The primary challenge involved dual-role management, requiring the design of a platform that allows seamless role-based access and management for both volunteers and organizations, ensuring that each user type could navigate their specific functionalities without confusion or security concerns. Additionally, the platform needed to incorporate sophisticated e-commerce and payment integration capabilities, ensuring secure, subscription-based payment flows for organizational partners while maintaining the highest standards of trust and compliance that are essential for nonprofit operations. The technical requirements extended beyond basic functionality to encompass advanced user experience features that would drive engagement and accessibility. Mobile optimization was crucial, guaranteeing a fully responsive experience across all devices, which was vital for on-the-go volunteer interactions and ensuring maximum participation regardless of device preferences. The platform also required real-time project matching capabilities, enabling users to search and apply for relevant opportunities by keyword, location, or category, creating an intuitive and efficient connection process between volunteers and organizations. Furthermore, comprehensive content engagement tools needed to be incorporated, including email marketing capabilities for newsletters, blogging functionality, and storytelling features designed to retain and inform users effectively. These multifaceted challenges required a robust, scalable solution that not only met complex technical needs but also aligned strategically with the client’s mission to make community service and debt relief more accessible to diverse populations.
approach: To address the multifaceted needs of Shared Harvest Fund, a comprehensive three-phase development approach was implemented, beginning with thorough ideation and UX design processes. During this initial phase, the development team created detailed user personas and journey maps to understand both volunteer and organization needs, ensuring that the platform would effectively serve its diverse user base. Interactive wireframes and clickable UI/UX prototypes were developed to iterate designs quickly and effectively, allowing for rapid testing and refinement of user interface concepts. The design phase maintained a strong focus on clean navigation and simplified workflows to achieve high usability standards, recognizing that ease of use would be critical for volunteer engagement and organizational adoption. The second phase involved custom platform development, where a bespoke WordPress site was built using PHP, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS to create a robust and scalable solution. The development team designed distinct user roles and dashboards specifically tailored for Debt-freelancers and Changemakers, ensuring that each user type could access relevant features and information efficiently. A comprehensive project board was implemented with advanced filtering capabilities for keyword, location, and project type searches, enabling precise matching between volunteers and opportunities. Secure payment processing was established through the integration of Stripe and PayPal for subscription-based payments, while content marketing tools were incorporated, including blog and storytelling modules alongside Mailchimp integration for email marketing and automated newsletters. The final phase encompassed launch, support, and optimization activities to ensure a successful platform deployment and ongoing performance. The site was hosted on Bluehost with reliable backup systems and scalable storage solutions to accommodate future growth. Thorough manual quality assurance testing was conducted to identify and resolve bugs before launch, ensuring a smooth user experience from day one. The platform was optimized for SEO readiness and mobile performance, guaranteeing accessibility across all devices and search engine visibility to maximize the platform’s reach and effectiveness in connecting volunteers with meaningful service opportunities.
outcome: 3x Application Speed - Streamlined the application process reduced submission time by 3x 100+ Projects Posted - Over 100 volunteer opportunities in the first 6 months $2.3 Million in Student Debt Relief Facilitated The launch of the new Shared Harvest Fund platform marked a major milestone in the organization’s ability to connect purpose with technology. By delivering a mobile-ready, role-based, and payment-integrated experience, the platform empowered users to participate in meaningful service engagements while reducing their student debt in a tangible way. Mobile Optimization Delivered Results The fully responsive design ensured a consistent, user-friendly experience across all device types, a critical need for the volunteer demographic. Post-launch analytics revealed a 45% increase in mobile session duration , with a 30% drop in bounce rates on mobile devices — indicating deeper engagement and ease of use on smartphones and tablets. Secure, Scalable E-commerce Infrastructure By integrating both Stripe and PayPal , the platform supported seamless, secure subscription payments for mission-driven organizations. This enhanced trust and reliability led to a 60% increase in paid partner sign-ups within the first 90 days of launch. The flexible billing model also reduced payment friction, contributing to a 25% reduction in user abandonment at the checkout stage. Improved User Participation and Workflow Efficiency The dual-role functionality and refined project-matching tools made it easier for volunteers to find and apply for service opportunities. As a result, there was a 50% increase in applications submitted through the platform. The admin team also reported a 35% reduction in manual intervention , thanks to automated user flows and dashboard-driven access, freeing up resources to focus on community growth. Content and Community Engagement Content tools like integrated blogs and Mailchimp-powered newsletters significantly boosted engagement. Shared stories of impact and mission updates reached a wide audience, with the newsletter achieving an impressive 42% open rate — outperforming industry averages by 18% . Additionally, blog posts shared via the platform generated a 23% uptick in repeat visitors , helping to strengthen the platform’s role as a hub for socially conscious professionals. Platform Performance and Scalability Built on WordPress and hosted on Bluehost , the platform handled increasing user traffic without performance degradation. SEO configurations led to improved search rankings, resulting in a 37% increase in organic traffic within six months. This positioned Shared Harvest Fund as a leader in the digital social impact space, with the technical foundation to grow sustainably. title: Transforming Workforce Development Through Modern Technology
excerpt: Discover how QualityWorks modernized workforce development with custom technology solutions—delivering streamlined training, enhanced engagement, and measurable performance improvements across teams.
customer: Knowledge Architects is a workforce development and training services firm that provides process improvement and training solutions to clients in the industrial and manufacturing sectors. They have developed and delivered a comprehensive set of mobile applications and interactive workforce solutions for some of the country’s largest and most complex transit systems. Their products and services include inspection apps, interactive learning content, and digital work instructions that prepare frontline workers for the operation and maintenance of new and existing equipment and systems.
challenge: Knowledge Architects faced critical challenges with their workforce training platform that were hampering their ability to serve industrial and manufacturing clients effectively. The company experienced significant technical performance problems that directly impacted system reliability and user satisfaction, with application quality standing at only 79% due to multiple failed test cases and critical bugs affecting core functionality. The 3D model loading time of 5 seconds created a poor user experience, while the complete absence of automated testing infrastructure left the platform vulnerable to recurring quality issues. These technical deficiencies were compounded by user experience challenges stemming from an outdated and inflexible interface that led to low user adoption rates, creating barriers to effective user engagement and platform utilization. The platform also suffered from critical functionality gaps and operational inefficiencies that hindered its effectiveness and administrative capabilities. Essential features such as user invitations and subscription management were completely absent from the system, and there was no admin dashboard available for subscription and user oversight, creating significant management challenges. Additionally, the platform experienced inefficient workflows in core operational areas, including user management and LMS (Learning Management System) functionality. These inefficiencies were further compounded by platform limitations, including a restrictive development environment that limited feature expansion opportunities, along with the lack of modern integrations and scalability options that constrained the platform’s ability to grow and adapt to evolving client needs.
approach: QualityWorks delivered a three-phase transformation that modernized Knowledge Architects’ workforce training platform through strategic technology upgrades and workflow redesign, addressing critical business challenges with measurable improvements. We established robust testing infrastructure with 318 new test cases and optimized 3D model performance, reducing load times from 5 to 3 seconds while increasing application quality from 79% to 98%. These improvements created a stable foundation for reliable user experiences. Our modern technology stack included Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and Shadcn UI for responsive frontend design, paired with Prisma ORM and CockroachDB for scalable data management. Infrastructure leveraged AWS S3, EC2, and Vercel for optimal performance, with strategic integrations including Auth.js, Stripe, Resend, and OpenAI for enhanced authentication, payments, communications, and AI-powered features. The complete platform rebuild transformed core workflows through redesigned user management, LMS, and subscription systems. We built a comprehensive admin dashboard with subscription monitoring, implemented role-based access control with user invitations, and added AI-powered personalized learning features, delivering a modern, scalable platform positioned for sustainable growth.
outcome: 40% Faster 3D model loading 25% Improvement in application quality 30% 3D Model Responsiveness Our platform transformation delivered exceptional outcomes across all performance indicators. Application quality improved 25% from 79% to 98%, while 3D model load times decreased 40% from 5 seconds to 3 seconds. Model responsiveness increased an average of 30% depending on complexity. Quality assurance metrics demonstrated excellence with 318 comprehensive test cases implemented from zero, complete elimination of 10 failed test cases, and resolution of 2 high-priority bugs. This testing infrastructure established sustained platform reliability. The transformation drove significant user engagement improvements with increased active users and higher task completion rates. Development efficiency improved through reduced cycles and fewer bugs, while subscription adoption increased and user churn decreased, demonstrating clear business value. Modern technology implementation resulted in faster page loads, enhanced security through robust authentication and data privacy compliance, and scalable architecture for future growth. AI-powered personalized learning features, combined with complete UI/UX overhaul and cross-platform compatibility, positioned Knowledge Architects with a cutting-edge workforce development platform ready for sustainable growth and enhanced user adoption.
